candidate.scope: The assigned Smart-Seq2 middle row of the Illumina single-cell poster: poly(A) mRNA, MMLV first-strand synthesis, LNA-associated template switching/cDNA synthesis, PCR, tagmentation and indexed DNA library completion. Smart-seq2 in the paper titles is the same named method. The separate Smart-Seq/NanoCAGE row above and partially cropped snRNA-Seq row below are neighboring poster entries, not connected alternatives of this assigned row. The top-edge DP-seq captions and right-edge LNA structural inset are contextual, not additional target workflows. This is a schematic-level architecture, not a complete laboratory protocol.

operations.description: Convert the depicted polyadenylated RNA into a first-strand cDNA associated with RNA; the drawn adapter-bearing oligo(dT) primes at the poly(A) end, and CCC appears at the other cDNA end.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Process amplified double-stranded cDNA into adapter-bearing cDNA fragment intermediates for final library completion.
operations.mechanism: Tagmentation is shown by paired blue enzyme icons at the cDNA. Fragmentation with adapter introduction is the interpretation of the named operation and its connection to the final indexed fragment; enzyme identity is not supplied here.

evidence.rationale: The term tagmentation identifies fragmentation with adapter tagging; the icons localize the processing to double-stranded cDNA and the downstream fragment carries terminal library regions. The enzyme is not named in this drawing.

operations.label: Gap repair, enrichment PCR and PCR purification
operations.description: Complete and amplify the tagmented cDNA fragments, then purify the resulting indexed DNA product shown with P5/P7 and Index 2/Index 1. The source combines these actions into one block. Although the output is captioned Enrichment-ready fragment, it is drawn after this combined block; no second enrichment operation is added.
operations.mechanism: The named combined block connects tagmentation to the final DNA fragment. The final end labels identify library adapters and indexes without specifying their oligonucleotide sequences.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert carries sequence copied from the polyadenylated RNA target, while P5/P7 and the two index regions define the displayed Illumina library interface. Sequencing this fragment population can support single-cell gene-expression profiling and coverage across represented transcripts. Full-length refers to the cDNA/coverage objective, not to every final DNA insert. The source protocol abstract reports lack of strand specificity and inability to detect poly(A)-negative RNA. The diagram gives no molecule-count barcode, cell barcode, pooling route or direct RNA readout.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title and the middle-row label identify Smart-Seq2. checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete scoped architecture: poly(A) RNA is copied into cDNA, the CCC/GGG/LNA template-switch interface provides the opposite priming end, PCR precedes tagmentation, and the combined completion block leads to indexed DNA. All five operations, six material states and ten flows agree at their interfaces. There is one in-scope route, no retained split, pooling operation or joint processing of independent branches. Adjacent rows are separate targets of other poster entries. The candidate retains the source captions, identifies the implicit tagmentation boundary, distinguishes full-length cDNA from fragment inserts, and records the protocol limitations. All fifteen publication leads and the literal poster reference are assessed at their available evidence levels. No consequential unsupported assertion, omitted transformation, paper-supported correction or blocking architecture question was found; acceptance is at schematic scope, not full experimental verification.
